title: Dedicated Fleet Entitlement and Approval Orchestration
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Define and implement an entitlement catalog and approval orchestration for dedicated capacity provisioning. This ticket covers the lifecycle from a capacity request (throughput commitment) through programmatic approval gates, autoscaling policy attachments, fleet assignment, and recording of an auditable decision trail. The goal is to reduce manual review time, standardize commitments, and ensure throughput guarantees map to SLOs and stock of fleet capacity. Deliverables: entitlement catalog schema, approval rules engine configuration, UI/UX for approvers in Console, integration points for autoscale policies and billing reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Entitlement catalog schema defined and published in Confluence (fields: customer_tier, min_tps, burst_credit, billing_profile, SLA_tier, required_documents)
Automated approval rules prototype implemented: low-risk requests auto-approve, medium-risk route to product ops, high-risk require legal/Sales sign-off
Console UI exposes a request card showing computed fleet fit, estimated provisioning time, cost delta, and suggested autoscale policy
Decision and audit trail persisted to audit-log store (searchable by request id) and surfaced in Console request history
End-to-end reservation request -> approval -> fleet assignment path completes within 48 hours for manual reviews and within 2 hours for auto-approved requests in staging
Associated autoscaling policy is attached on approval and exercised in a canary (2-hour ramp) with metrics reported to the capacity dashboard
work_items: Draft entitlement catalog fields and example templates (PM + Eng review)
Implement approval rules engine config (feature-flagged) and integration tests
Add request visualization card in Console (design + front-end)
Hook approval outcome to Fleet API to reserve capacity and attach autoscaling policy
Emit audit log entries for every state transition (requested, evaluated, approved, rejected, assigned)
Create staging end-to-end runbook and load-test the auto-approval heuristics
notes: Avoid free-form 'reservation' objects in DB; use normalized entitlement records so approvals can be replayed and re-evaluated after policy changes.
Autoscaling policy attachment should be an idempotent operation: re-applying the same policy must not create duplicate schedules or alerts.
We will default to conservative fleet-fit calculations and include a 15% buffer for overhead and unexpected traffic patterns.
Billing impact: approved throughput must generate a billing ticket (line item) and be reconcilable to usage reports for the month.
Fallback strategy: if assigned fleet cannot honor guaranteed throughput, system will mark request as 'degraded' and trigger automatic mitigation (burstable fallback and customer notification)
Cross-functional reviewers: Product Ops, Infra SRE, Billing, Legal (for contracts), and Sales for strategic accounts
